items.excerpt: Here’s a rundown of all the news you need to start your Thursday, including Israel’s final vote count, renewed efforts to revive US-Iran talks, Spain mourning one of its deadliest train crashes, North Korea’s missile launches, and Flavio Bolsonaro declaring himself Brazil’s “leader” from the US. More than 500,000 outstanding ballots could reshape Israel’s parliamentary seat distribution as counting continues Thursday, with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc nor its main opposition projected to secure a governing majority. Netanyahu’s bloc was projected to win 53 seats, compared with 48 for the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot and a record combined 19 for predominantly Arab parties, according to Channel 12. A majority requires 61 seats in the 120-member Knesset. The outstanding ballots, cast by soldiers and others voting away from their registered polling stations, were expected to be counted by Thursday evening, Israel’s public broadcaster reported. - Trump confirms Vance’s Iran contact as regional powers push for deal President Donald Trump said Washington is communicating with Iran through mediators, as regional governments seek to revive peace negotiations and avert renewed US strikes. The Wall Street Journal reported that Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei at Trump’s direction. Asked about the contact, Trump said he had approved Vance’s request to help Iran obtain medical supplies. “Basically, it’s getting supplies in to help people that are not well,” he said. Qatar-led mediators are urging Tehran to allow UN inspectors into bombed nuclear sites in exchange for some US sanctions relief, Axios reported. Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Türkiye are supporting the effort. Trump said he did not know whether negotiations would succeed. Trump also had a phone call with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, who told him that the Mecca Joint Defense Alliance was closely monitoring developments in the Strait of Hormuz and Yemen. - Spain begins three days of mourning after deadly train crash Spain is in three days of mourning after Wednesday's collision between two high-speed trains killed at least 68 people, one of the worst rail disasters in Europe's recent history. Speaking at the crash site in Toledo, Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said authorities would determine the cause of the accident and take action if wrongdoing was uncovered. Sanchez said it was "unacceptable" for a country like Spain to experience two high-speed rail accidents in a single year, referring to January's deadly derailment that claimed the lives of 46 people. "We will get to the bottom of this. If there has been negligence, it will be known," he said, according to Spanish news agency EFE. - Tensions rise as North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles North Korea launched around a dozen short-range ballistic missiles from the Wonsan area toward the East Sea, also known as the Sea of Japan, on Thursday, South Korea’s military said. Seoul stepped up surveillance for further launches and shared information with the US and Japan as officials assessed the missiles’ flight distances and other details, Yonhap News reported.

items.excerpt: Israelis await final election results as claim of foreign interference emerges JERUSALEM (AP) — Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his party have amplified claims that the country's election was “stolen” by Arab-led parties. Final results are expected to confirm on Thursday that Netanyahu's bloc has lost its majority in parliament. The opposition accuses Netanyahu of demonizing the Arab population after a strong showing by Arab-led parties. If the opposition teams up with those parties in a rare and politically risky move, they could form the next government. The elections committee has asked the Shin Bet intelligence service to investigate alleged election interference by unspecified “foreign entities.” Netanyahu's Likud party targeted Arab-led parties even before the vote, despite lacking specific evidence. URDA, Spain (AP) — Spain faces fresh concerns about rail safety after a second high-speed train crash this year killed 69 people. Search teams using sniffer dogs continued to look for victims on Thursday morning a day after the collision in central Spain. One more body was found overnight. The collision Wednesday involved a RENFE train striking a stationary IRYO train in Toledo. This crash comes just weeks before a national election, adding pressure on Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's government. Spain's transport minister said human error caused the latest crash. Unions pushed back against the minister. Three days of national mourning started Thursday. The expansion in third-quarter gross domestic product – the nation’s output of goods and services – was faster than the 2.2% growth registered from April through June, the Commerce Department said Thursday. Hey, Milwaukee: grab a brat, raise a beer and prepare for that parade. Young ace Jacob Misiorowski threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings of two-hit ball, rookie Cooper Pratt got two more hits and two RBIs, and Milwaukee beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 to set off a long-awaited celebration among thousands of Brewers fans in attendance at Tropicana Field. items.title: PCE inflation report September 2026:
items.excerpt: Published Thu, Oct 29 2026 8:32 AM EDT Updated 42 Min Ago ... Key Points - The U.S. economy grew at a 3.4% pace in the third quarter, faster than expected. - Inflation continued to run above the Fed's 2% target in September, with a headline rate of 3.6% and core at 3.1%, according to the central bank's preferred gauge. - Consumer spending was slightly below forecasts, though still up 0.5%. Personal income increased just 0.2%. ... The pace of price increases stepped up in September, keeping inflation well above the Federal Reserve's target, while the economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter, according to Commerce Department reports Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures price index increased a seasonally adjusted 0.5% for the month, putting the annual inflation rate at 3.6%. The monthly increase was the largest since March but in line with the Dow Jones consensus, while the annual rate was 0.1 percentage point below. Excluding food and energy, the core PCE posted respective readings of 0.3% and 3.1%, in line with the consensus. While the Fed follows both measures closely, officials generally see the core reading as more indicative of longer-term inflation trends. While inflation continued to run ahead of the Fed's 2% target, the Commerce Department also reported that gross domestic product was strong in the third quarter. GDP increased at a seasonally adjusted annualized pace of 3.4%, better than the 3.1% estimate and well ahead of the 2.2% in the second quarter. Also, in September consumer spending proved resilient, climbing 0.5%, a bit below the forecast for a 0.6% gain, while personal income rose 0.2%, compared with the estimate for 0.3%. The reports come the day after the Fed voted to hold its benchmark interest rate in a range between 3.75%-4%. Despite elevated inflation readings, central bank officials insist they can afford to evaluate incoming data before deciding on their next move. "The period right in front of us is information rich. There is a lot that's happening in the world. My colleagues and I are keen to take notice of it," Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said Wednesday. However, the data deluge from Thursday shows the Fed could have more work to do. A Labor Department report also released Thursday showed that layoffs remain low. Initial jobless claims edged lower to a seasonally adjusted 194,000 for the week ended Oct. 24, below the estimate for 200,000 and near levels last seen in the late 1960s. ... Economic growth has been driven by higher levels of investment from the artificial intelligence build-out, as well as high levels of consumer and government spending. Consumer spending rose 3.8% in the third quarter, the same pace as the prior period. Gross private domestic investment soared 19.4%, driven by a 20.9% surge in equipment spending and an 8.4% jump on intellectual property products. Real sales to private domestic purchasers, a proxy that Fed officials use for underlying demand, rose 4.9%, compared with a 4.6% increase in the second quarter. There was some good inflation news for the period: On a quarterly basis, PCE prices rose 2.1% on the headline number and 2.5% for core, down respectively from 5% and 3.3% in the second quarter. September's price increases were driven largely by a surge in energy costs that economists fear could be spreading to other parts of the economy. Gasoline and other energy goods saw a 9.2% rise for the month while energy goods and services broadly jumped 5.4%. At the same time, services prices excluding energy and housing rose 0.4%, and housing costs increased 0.3%.

items.excerpt: - AP - Oct 29, 2026 - Oct 29, 2026 Updated 2 hrs ago ... Hometown of ‘Addams Family’ creator becomes ghoulish Halloween destination WESTFIELD, N.J. (AP) — The New Jersey town that helped birth “The Addams Family” is embracing its ghoulish legacy. Westfield is the hometown of Charles Addams, the cartoonist who created the darkly eccentric, fictional family. Addams drew inspiration for his signature macabre style from the elegant Victorian homes, historic cemetery and other landmarks of the town just outside New York City. Every October, the town hosts AddamsFest with events that include an art exhibit, music festival, masquerade ball and other events. A self-guided heritage trail takes visitors past landmarks that informed Addams’ creations, including a Victorian-era house that helped inspire the fictional family's imposing, gothic abode. South Carolina police close investigation into Hayden Panettiere's death after coroner's ruling Police in South Carolina say they have closed their investigation into the overdose death of actor Hayden Panettiere following a coroner’s findings that it was accidental. No charges were filed. Greenville police said Wednesday in a statement the decision was based on the medical examiner’s determination as well as the findings of the investigation. The former star of the TV series “Heroes” and “Nashville” was pronounced dead in an apartment in Greenville on Aug. 16 at age 36 after paramedics found her unresponsive. It remains unclear whether federal agents are still looking into her death separately. A serial killer, an obsessed cop and an undercover FBI agent. The series is based on Lars Kepler novels. It premieres Friday. It follows a kidnapped teen who resurfaces after three years, while his sister remains missing. Graham plays Jurek Walter, an imprisoned murderer who manipulates those around him. The show features a retired detective, played by Liev Schreiber, and an undercover FBI agent, portrayed by Zazie Beetz. The creators aim to offer a fresh take on the genre. ... California appeals court upholds actor Danny Masterson's rape convictions LOS ANGELES (AP) — A California appeals court has upheld actor Danny Masterson’s convictions and long prison sentence for raping two women at his home in 2003. The three-judge panel on Tuesday unanimously found that the “That ’70s Show” actor had failed to demonstrate that the lower court made errors that would warrant granting him a new trial. Masterson was convicted in 2023 of raping two women at his home two decades earlier. He was sentenced to 30 years to life in prison. His attorneys said in an emailed statement Tuesday that they would seek review at the California Supreme Court. Russell Brand denies all charges as he takes the stand at his rape and sex assault trial LONDON (AP) — Russell Brand says allegations of sexual misconduct have had a “devastating” impact on his life. The actor and comedian testified in court Wednesday at his trial on charges of rape and sexual assault. Brand, 51, denied all charges, stating that friends and colleagues have abandoned him. He also mentioned being barred from staying with his baby son in the hospital due to the allegations. Over the past two weeks, prosecutors have presented their case, with six women accusing Brand of misconduct between 1999 and 2009. Brand insists that consent is fundamental, denying any wrongdoing. Laurence Rupp plays her partner and the father of her young child and is under investigation for child sex abuse and participating in online forums. In her review for The Associated Press, film writer Lindsey Bahr praises Seydoux's understated and searing performance, as well as the film's handling of a difficult topic. Bahr writes that it is a film that wants you to question your own complicity. Rated R, “Gentle Monster” is in select theaters Friday. Iran sentences acclaimed film director Jafar Panahi to new prison term after his return home CAIRO (AP) — Iran has sentenced acclaimed film director Jafar Panahi to five years and one month in prison, following his return to the country earlier this year, after the start of U.S. and Israeli attacks on the Islamic Republic. The Tehran court also ordered the confiscation of Panahi’s “movable and immovable assets.” That's according to his lawyer Mostafa Nili, who spoke in an interview with the reformist news site Emtedad on Tuesday. Nili did not say what Panahi was convicted of. But the director, who returned to Iran in March, had been previously convicted of “propaganda activities against the system.”

items.excerpt: MultiChoice has cut movie repeats across DStv’s channels by 40%, Canal+ Africa chief content officer Nomsa Philiso told MyBroadband. The South African pay-TV giant achieved this by shutting down certain channels and moving their exclusive content elsewhere on its platform. In September, MultiChoice South Africa announced the biggest overhaul of DStv’s products in 15 years, including the creation of a Sports and Movies & Series package. The shake-up included several changes to DStv channels. Most significantly, it shut down 4 entertainment channels and moved several others to lower-tier packages. Mzansi Wethu (DStv 163) was rebranded as Wethu+. It combined Mzansi Wethu’s existing content with programming from Mzansi Bioskop and Mzansi Magic Music, which were shut down.
